title: Aston Martin ends F1 testing program early, capping off nightmare preseason for team
content:
SAKHIR, Bahrain — Aston Martin called an early end to its Formula 1 testing program in Bahrain on Friday due to a shortage of engine parts, concluding what has been a nightmare preseason for the team.

After only making it to the first private test in Barcelona for the penultimate day of running at the end of January, Aston Martin’s struggles with its new car have continued through the past two weeks at the Bahrain International Circuit.

Fernando Alonso stopped out on the track early in the afternoon session on Thursday due to an issue with his Honda engine, bringing his day to an early end.

Honda issued a statement on Friday morning saying it was a “battery-related issue” and that it had since been completing simulations on its engine test bench at its base in Sakura, Japan.

“Due to this and a shortage of power unit parts, we have adapted today’s run plan to be very limited and consist only of very short runs.”

The running came to a total of only six laps, all completed by Lance Stroll and without setting a time, before a team spokesperson announced it had completed its program for the day.

The setbacks leave Aston Martin firmly on the back foot ahead of the new F1 season, which starts with the Australian Grand Prix on March 8.

Pedro de la Rosa, a former F1 driver and Aston Martin’s team representative, told F1 TV on Friday that it was “definitely we are not where we wanted to be” going into the new campaign due to its lack of mileage.

“We have been the team with the (fewest) laps during preseason testing,” said De la Rosa. “We would have preferred to do a lot more, but despite the fact that we haven’t done a lot of laps, we have an enormous amount of data to look into and to prepare ourselves for Australia.”

The Aston Martin team, which is owned by Canadian billionaire Lawrence Stroll, had long identified 2026 and the overhaul of F1’s technical regulations as being a big landmark in its ambitions to become capable of fighting for world championships in the future.

Besides the start of its partnership with Honda, Aston Martin has invested heavily in a state-of-the-art factory at Silverstone in the UK, as well as signing Adrian Newey, the most successful car designer in F1 history, to join last year from Red Bull.

Newey was appointed team principal for the 2026 season, but revealed in a recent interview with the team’s website that the new car project was four months behind schedule at one stage, causing it to miss the majority of the running in Barcelona.

When the car did hit the track, it sported a radical aerodynamic design that caught the attention of its rivals, only for its limited mileage and lack of performance through testing to suggest the team will start the new season toward the very back of the grid.

Alonso, a two-time F1 world champion, admitted last week the team was “on the slow side and on the back foot,” while Stroll stated at one point that it looked around four seconds slower than the leading teams.

After completing 206 laps across last week’s three-day test in Bahrain last week, Aston Martin managed only 128 across the final set of running this week, equivalent to just over two race distances.

On Friday, the team announced that it had acquired the rights to use the Aston Martin name, logo and branding as part of an agreement with the manufacturer, which is a separate company to the F1 team but has Stroll as a majority owner.
